ledger.claim: The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00528, and the trace's first fix (2026-09-16T08:16:40+08:00) matches the trip_record's started_at, so limb (a) of POL-RD-08 is satisfied: the artifacts describe one and the same trip, and the rider is entitled to have this dispute decided on them rather than on the characterisation in the claim text.

The driver's own trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 229 fixes at a 10-second sampling cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required, and the trace distance of 22.26 km is the governing POL-RD-01 measurement in place of the rounded trip_record copy of 22.3 km.

Measured on that governing figure the excess is 0.16 km, which is 0.72% of the 22.1 km optimal route: it fails BOTH POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km absolute and greater than 20% relative). The rider does not press a deviation the trace cannot carry, no exculpatory clause needs to be reached because there is no excess to excuse, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation is not triggered on this record.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory covering this trip: EV-ADVIS-00528-01 is MISSING, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and its absence is itself citable. That cuts against, not for, the driver, because his statement invokes no exculpatory clause and cites no evidence ID for an advisory; an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, so the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger, under POL-RD-13 limb (1), and POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all without an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses.

The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantry crossings and no tolls (both totals are 0.00) and an airport_surcharge of 0.0 on a trip that neither originates at nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom or double-counted pass-through line, and no gantry line to match against the trace under POL-RD-09 limb (4). That limb is the one route POL-RD-01 leaves open when the establishment tests fail, and on this record it is empty.

The governing measurement for the threshold test is the trace polyline: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 22.26 km, and the platform's own derived deviation block records an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.72% of the 22.1 km optimal route, with the status field reading 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass — an excess greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal. An excess of 0.16 km fails the absolute test five-fold and 0.72% fails the proportional test by a wide margin. No route deviation is established on this trip.

POL-RD-01 forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, but the driver's position does not depend on that rule: even on the rounded field the rider's side would prefer (22.3 km, deviation_pct 0.9 as recorded on the trip record), the excess over the 22.1 km optimal is 0.2 km — a quarter of the 0.8 km absolute threshold — and under 1% against a 20% proportional threshold. On either figure the establishment test fails on both limbs, and POL-RD-01 provides that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The trace is unimpaired both at the schema level (EV-GPS-00528 is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes) and for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of limbs (a) to (c) — a gap over 90 seconds, a jump over 500 m, a sustained interval over 30 seconds — is met. The excess is therefore measured from a full-strength trace, no independent corroboration is needed, and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not open.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show both that the artifacts describe the same trip and that an excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The second limb fails on every artifact in the bundle — the excess is 0.16 km on the trace and 0.2 km even on the rounded trip-record figure — so the burden never shifts to the driver: he is not required to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12, and an assertion of overcharging that no artifact supports carries no weight.

There is no traffic advisory on file at all: EV-ADVIS-00528-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, has weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING) — that impairment is disclosed, and the artifact can carry no fact; its absence is all that is citable. The driver asserts no queue, closure or incident — his statement on the record is 'Normal trip, normal route. I don't set fares.' — so POL-RD-03 is never invoked and there is no external-cause assertion to test against an advisory. Under POL-RD-13 an advisory that no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not the contradiction with a cited artifact that POL-RD-10(5) escalates on; the missing advisory therefore changes nothing and triggers no escalation.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity line for POL-RD-09(4) to act on: the fare ledger carries erp_gantries [] with tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, and the derived erp_lines block totals 0.00 on-route and 0.00 off-route. Nothing in the fare is a phantom gantry or a wrongly applied surcharge, so there is no standalone correction to make with or without a deviation.

With no deviation established, POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION, and POL-GEN-03 fixes what that means on this record: the present state stands. The ledger records payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and charged_total SGD 44.44. This dispute was filed by the rider, so leaving the present state in place leaves the fare charged and unrefunded — which is the driver's case, not the rider's.

The rider's account of the money matches no artifact: he pleads a SGD 60 estimate and a SGD 91.60 charge, and says a manager refunded the difference plus a voucher, but the fare breakdown shows charged_total SGD 44.44, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED, and the chat export for this trip contains zero messages. The fare that does exist is internally consistent — base fare 3.80 plus distance 16.73 plus time 10.64 plus the 0.80 platform fee plus surge 12.47 equals 44.44 exactly. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no supporting artifact carries no weight.

The rider's 'no surge' complaint is a complaint about the fare model, not about the route. The surge_multiplier of 1.4 is recorded on EV-FARE-00528 — the only artifact from which the policy permits that figure to be read — and it is applied to base fare, distance charge and time charge, producing the SGD 12.47 surge line. No clause of the route-deviation policy refunds a correctly applied surge where no deviation is established, and POL-RD-02's recomputation does not run at all without one.

Nothing in the driver's record assists the rider. POL-RD-06 is not engaged, because it is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation or the evidence is otherwise finely balanced, and neither condition holds here; and its own counters are silent in any event — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, far below both the '3 or more' limb and the 5% limb. No profile field other than those POL-RD-06 names may be used against him (POL-GEN-01).

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the decisive route measurements. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00528 (weight 1.0) records 22.26 km, and the booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-00528 (weight 1.0) is 22.1 km. The excess is 0.16 km, or 0.72% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires both an excess greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal to establish a route deviation. Neither test is met, so no deviation exists and NO_ACTION follows. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, and max_gap_sec 0.0, so no independent corroboration issue arises. There are no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines to correct under POL-RD-09: the fare ledger EV-FARE-00528 (weight 1.0) shows tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, and derived ERP totals of 0.00 on and off the optimal route. The fare ledger shows charged_total SGD 44.44, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00, and surge_multiplier 1.4 read from the fare breakdown; no route-deviation clause refunds that correctly applied surge where no deviation is established. The rider's account of a SGD 91.60 charge and a manager refund plus voucher is not supported by any artifact: the chat log EV-CHAT-00528 contains zero messages and the ledger records no refund issued, so under POL-RD-08 that account carries no weight. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00528-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is noted, but no party invoked POL-RD-03 and the driver asserted no external traffic cause, so it is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; POL-RD-13 confirms no escalation on that point. The driver profile was not used as a ground of decision, POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and its citable counters show no pattern. No clause produces a referral. The present state stands: the fare remains charged and unrefunded, and no driver compensation is due.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
